claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi's component state migrations are new.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion at pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799 exists for component state migrations feedback.

The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component referring to the VPC.
Replacing an AWS VPC would require replacing the security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId docs).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The example does not create a database.
The second version of the example upgrades to the modern `awsx.ec2.Vpc` component while keeping the existing network.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
Resource trees: v1 has awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with Subnet and InternetGateway component wrappers; v2 has awsx:ec2:Vpc with aws resources directly under it; v3 has plain aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc as root.
Each Pulumi state record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID such as an AWS VPC ID.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents.
In the example, the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
A component registers a migration callback through the `stateMigrations` resource option, together with an alias for the legacy component type.

The state migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (the complete set of replacement records) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The migration callback is idempotent: if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid after migration.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and maps both the old component and its VPC child to the new VPC record, which keeps its AWS ID.

Pulumi runs state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS; a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration; after both have run, callbacks return no result on later updates.

After a migration changes saved state, Pulumi compares the new program with that state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
Before each upgrade in the example, the preview should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.

When users upgrade a component that registers a migration internally, Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of normal preview and update without users writing the migration or attaching the callback.
The VPC example at pulumi/examples aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration contains all three programs and migration code; the state migrations guide covers the callback contract.
State migration callbacks (the Pulumi resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi stateMigrations resource option reference documents the callback API at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api.
Component state migration entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
